% Quarantined P07.1 research candidate, 30 August 2026.
% This file is not a live-book input, has not received independent review,
% and has not been submitted to production Rethlas.  No novelty or priority
% claim is made.

Let \(Z\) be a locally compact Hausdorff space with a basis of clopen
subsets.  Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real affine space, let
\(P\subset E\) be a nonempty convex polyhedron, possibly unbounded and
possibly of dimension smaller than \(E\), and put
\(A=\operatorname{Aff}(P)\).  Set
\[
                              X=Z\times P .
\]

We use the following smooth psh generator sheaf on \(X\).  A real-valued
function \(f\) on an open subset of \(X\) is smooth if, locally at every
\((z,x)\), there are a clopen neighbourhood \(D\) of \(z\), an open
neighbourhood \(O\) of \(x\) in \(A\), and \(F\in C^\infty(O)\) such that
\[
                  f(z',x')=F(x')
       \quad\text{on }D\times(P\cap O).
\]
It is a smooth psh generator if the Hessian of \(F\) is positive
semidefinite at every point of \(P\cap O\).  Denote this sheaf by
\(\operatorname{Psh}_{X,0}\), denote by
\(\operatorname{Psh}_{X,1}\) its first local pointwise-decreasing-limit
stage, and denote by \(\operatorname{Psh}_X\) the smallest subsheaf of
\(\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\)-valued functions which contains
\(\operatorname{Psh}_{X,0}\) and is stable under local pointwise decreasing
limits of sequences.

Define \(\mathscr C_X\) by the following local condition.  A section \(u\)
belongs to \(\mathscr C_X\) near \((z_0,x_0)\) if there are
\begin{itemize}
\item a compact clopen neighbourhood \(C\subset Z\) of \(z_0\);
\item a relatively open convex neighbourhood \(V\subset P\) of \(x_0\);
\item a compact metrizable zero-dimensional space \(Y\) and a continuous
  surjection \(q:C\twoheadrightarrow Y\); and
\item an upper semicontinuous function
  \(\bar u:Y\times V\to\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\)
\end{itemize}
such that
\begin{equation}
 u(z,x)=\bar u(q(z),x),
 \qquad
 x\longmapsto\bar u(y,x)\text{ is extended-real convex for every }y\in Y.
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-factorization}
\end{equation}
Here extended-real convexity uses no \(+\infty\) values and omits terms
with zero coefficient.

Then \(\mathscr C_X\) is a sheaf and
\begin{equation}
             \operatorname{Psh}_{X,1}
             =\operatorname{Psh}_X
             =\mathscr C_X.
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-collapse}
\end{equation}
More precisely, if \(u\in\operatorname{Psh}_X(W)\) and
\((z_0,x_0)\in W\), there are a compact clopen neighbourhood
\(C\ni z_0\), a relatively open polyhedral neighbourhood \(V\ni x_0\),
and smooth psh functions \(G_k\in\operatorname{Psh}_{X,0}(C\times V)\)
such that
\begin{equation}
                         G_{k+1}\leq G_k,
             \qquad      G_k\longrightarrow u|_{C\times V}
             \quad\text{pointwise}.
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-fixed-domain}
\end{equation}

The same conclusion holds on every Hausdorff space equipped with a
generator sheaf which is locally identified, by generator-preserving
charts, with one of the preceding product models.  In particular it holds
on locally finite polyhedral manifolds with corners, with an arbitrary
locally compact clopen-base transverse parameter carrying only locally
constant affine directions.

For the standing \(K=\mathbf Q\), \(G=\mathbf R\) conventions of
Chambert--Loir--Ducros, a rational polyhedron \(P\) with its induced
affine tropical structure and \(Z\) with its locally constant affine
structure give the displayed generator sheaf through their product
construction.  The assertion is confined to this convex single-chamber
model.  It makes no claim for a nonconvex union of chambers, a branched
polyhedral complex, nonconstant affine directions on \(Z\), or an
arbitrary affine \(G\)-tropical space.  It therefore narrows but does not
retire P07.1.

% Book-local finite-star polyhedral product theorem, 10 September 2026.
% It concerns only the explicitly defined ambient-induced generator sheaf.
% No priority claim is made.
\begin{theorem}[Finite ambient stars with polyhedral Euclidean directions]
\label{thm:p071-finite-star-polyhedral-collapse}
Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space and let
\[
 S=\{0\}\cup\coprod_{i=1}^{m}(0,r_i)v_i\subset E,
 \qquad 1\leq m<\infty,
\]
where \(r_i>0\), \(v_i\ne0\), and the positive rays
\(\mathbf R_{>0}v_i\) are pairwise distinct.  Let \(P\) be a nonempty
convex polyhedron in a finite-dimensional real affine space; write
\(A:=\operatorname{Aff}(P)\).  Thus \(P\) may be unbounded or
zero-dimensional.  Put \(X:=S\times P\).
For an ordinary open \(W\subset X\), let \(\mathcal G_{X,0}(W)\) be the
real-valued functions which are locally restrictions of smooth ambient
functions on \(E\times A\) and for which, on every branch, the function
\[
 (t,y)\longmapsto g(tv_i,y)
\]
has positive-semidefinite full Hessian in the \((t,y)\) variables wherever
it is defined.  Let \(\mathcal P_{X,1}\) be the sheaf of local pointwise
decreasing limits of sequences in \(\mathcal G_{X,0}\), and let
\(\mathcal P_X\) be the smallest subsheaf of
\(\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\)-valued functions which contains
\(\mathcal G_{X,0}\) and is closed under such limits.

Let \(\mathcal J_X(W)\) consist of the functions
\(u:W\to\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\) with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item for every branch \(i\), the function obtained by setting
      \(u_i(0,y):=u(0,y)\) and \(u_i(t,y):=u(tv_i,y)\) for \(t>0\)
      is extended-real jointly convex on every convex subset of
      \[
       \{(t,y)\in[0,r_i)\times P:(tv_i,y)\in W\};
      \]
\item whenever \((0,y_0)\in W\), finitely many points
      \((t_av_{i(a)},y_a)\in W\), and numbers \(\alpha_a\geq0\) satisfy
      \[
       \sum_a\alpha_a=1,
       \qquad
       \sum_a\alpha_at_av_{i(a)}=0,
       \qquad
       \sum_a\alpha_ay_a=y_0,
      \]
      and every segment from \((0,y_0)\) to a point with
      \(\alpha_a>0\) is contained in \(W\), then
      \[
       u(0,y_0)\leq\sum_a\alpha_a u(t_av_{i(a)},y_a).
       \tag{\(\mathrm J_{S\times P}\)}
      \]
      Terms with zero coefficient are omitted from the extended-real sum.
\end{enumerate}
Then \(\mathcal J_X\) is a sheaf and
\[
                       \mathcal P_{X,1}=\mathcal P_X=\mathcal J_X.
\]
More precisely, every germ in these sheaves has a pointwise decreasing
approximation by members of \(\mathcal G_{X,0}\) on one fixed smaller
neighbourhood.  At a point of \(\{0\}\times P\), that neighbourhood may
be chosen to be the product of a smaller finite substar and a relatively
open polyhedral neighbourhood in \(P\).
\end{theorem}

% Book-local P07.1 theorem, 13 September 2026.
% This theorem combines the locally constant Stone-parameter mechanism with
% the finite ambient-star x convex-polyhedron mechanism.  It makes no
% novelty or priority claim.
\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:p071-stone-finite-star-polyhedral-collapse}
Let \(Z\) be a locally compact Hausdorff space with a basis of clopen
subsets.  Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space and let
\[
 S=\{0\}\cup\coprod_{i=1}^{m}(0,r_i)v_i\subset E,
 \qquad 1\leq m<\infty,
\]
where \(r_i>0\), \(v_i\ne0\), and the positive rays
\(\mathbf R_{>0}v_i\) are pairwise distinct.  Let \(P\) be a nonempty
convex polyhedron in a finite-dimensional real affine space, put
\(A=\operatorname{Aff}(P)\), and set
\[
                              X=Z\times S\times P.
\]

For an ordinary open \(W\subset X\), let \(\mathcal G_{X,0}(W)\) be the
real-valued functions with the following local description.  After
shrinking the \(Z\)-variable to a clopen neighbourhood, the function is
independent of that variable and is the restriction of a smooth ambient
function on \(E\times A\) whose restriction
\[
                 (t,y)\longmapsto g(tv_i,y)
\]
has positive-semidefinite full Hessian on every branch chamber on which it
is defined.  Let \(\mathcal P_{X,1}\) be the sheaf of local pointwise
decreasing limits of sequences in \(\mathcal G_{X,0}\), and let
\(\mathcal P_X\) be the smallest subsheaf of
\(\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\)-valued functions which contains
\(\mathcal G_{X,0}\) and is closed under such limits.

Define \(\mathcal C_X\) by the following local condition.  A section \(u\)
belongs to \(\mathcal C_X\) near \((z_0,0,y_0)\) if, after shrinking to a
product of a compact clopen neighbourhood \(C\ni z_0\), a smaller finite
substar \(S'\ni0\), and a relatively open convex neighbourhood
\(V\ni y_0\) in \(P\), there are a compact metrizable zero-dimensional
space \(Y\), a continuous surjection \(q:C\twoheadrightarrow Y\), and an
upper semicontinuous function
\[
        \bar u:Y\times S'\times V
             \longrightarrow\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}
\]
such that
\begin{equation}
 u(z,s,y)=\bar u(q(z),s,y),
 \label{eq:p071-stone-star-factorization}
\end{equation}
and, for every \(\zeta\in Y\), the function
\(\bar u_\zeta(s,y):=\bar u(\zeta,s,y)\) satisfies:
\begin{enumerate}
\item on each branch, with the common value at \(t=0\), the function
  \((t,y)\mapsto\bar u_\zeta(tv_i,y)\) is extended-real jointly convex on
  every convex subset of its domain;
\item for every finite family of points
  \((t_av_{i(a)},y_a)\) and weights \(\alpha_a\geq0\) whose joining
  segments from \((0,y_*)\) remain in the domain and which satisfy
  \[
    \sum_a\alpha_a=1,
    \qquad \sum_a\alpha_at_av_{i(a)}=0,
    \qquad \sum_a\alpha_ay_a=y_*,
  \]
  one has the product junction inequality
  \begin{equation}
     \bar u_\zeta(0,y_*)
        \leq\sum_a\alpha_a
                    \bar u_\zeta(t_av_{i(a)},y_a).
   \label{eq:p071-stone-star-junction}
  \end{equation}
  Terms with zero coefficient are omitted from the extended-real sum.
\end{enumerate}
Away from the node, the same definition is used after restricting to the
single branch containing the point; condition
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-star-junction} is then vacuous.

Then \(\mathcal C_X\) is a sheaf and
\begin{equation}
                 \mathcal P_{X,1}=\mathcal P_X=\mathcal C_X.
 \label{eq:p071-stone-star-collapse}
\end{equation}
More precisely, every germ in these sheaves has a pointwise decreasing
approximation by members of \(\mathcal G_{X,0}\) on one fixed smaller
product neighbourhood.  At a node point \((z_0,0,y_0)\), the neighbourhood
may be chosen as \(C\times S''\times V'\), where \(C\) is compact clopen,
\(S''\) is a finite substar with one positive collar on every branch, and
\(V'\) is a relatively open polyhedral neighbourhood in \(P\).

The theorem permits simultaneously a nonmetrizable Stone parameter,
genuine finite branching, nonconstant affine directions, and all faces and
corners of one convex polyhedron.  It concerns the displayed product
generator sheaf.  It makes no assertion for nonconstant affine directions
on the Stone factor, an infinite non-CLD star, separately convex
generators, a nonambient branch structure, or a nonconvex chamber gluing.
Consequently it narrows but does not retire P07.1.
\end{theorem}
proof:
% Quarantined proof corresponding exactly to statement.tex.
% It is not a live-book input and has not received production verification.

\begin{proof}
We first isolate three elementary points which will be used twice.

\medskip\noindent\emph{Local extended-real convexity on a convex set.}
Let \(H\) be a convex subset of a finite-dimensional affine space and let
\(v:H\to\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\) be locally extended-real convex.  Then
\(v\) is extended-real convex on \(H\).  It is enough to restrict to a
segment and prove the assertion on an interval \(I\).  On
\(I^\circ\), both
\[
 \{t:v(t)\in\mathbf R\}
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \{t:v(t)=-\infty\}
\]
are open.  For the first set, if a finite point had arbitrarily close
\(-\infty\) points, write the finite point as a strict convex combination
of one of them and a point on its other side, inside one interval of local
convexity.  For the second set, if \(v(t)=-\infty\), then every sufficiently
nearby \(s\) lies strictly between \(t\) and another point of the same
local convexity interval; the convexity inequality forces
\(v(s)=-\infty\).  Connectedness of \(I^\circ\) shows that \(v\) is either
finite throughout \(I^\circ\) or identically \(-\infty\) there.

In the first case an included endpoint cannot have value \(-\infty\):
local convexity there would propagate \(-\infty\) to a one-sided interior
collar.  Thus \(v\) is finite on \(I\), and the usual subdivision argument
applies: on a partition fine enough that each pair of consecutive
subintervals lies in a local convexity interval, the successive secant
slopes are nondecreasing.  Summing the slope inequalities proves global
convexity.  In the second case every convexity inequality at a point of
\(I^\circ\) has left side \(-\infty\), while the endpoint cases are
tautological.  This proves the assertion, including possible finite values
at the two endpoints of an otherwise polar segment.

\medskip\noindent\emph{Continuous convexification on a polytope.}
Let \(K\) be a compact convex polytope in a \(d\)-dimensional affine space
and let \(\phi:K\to\mathbf R\) be continuous.  Put
\begin{equation}
 (\operatorname{co}_K\phi)(x)
 =
 \inf\left\{
       \sum_i\alpha_i\phi(x_i):
       \alpha_i\geq0,\ \sum_i\alpha_i=1,\
       \sum_i\alpha_i x_i=x
      \right\}.
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-convex-envelope}
\end{equation}
This is the largest convex function on \(K\) bounded above by \(\phi\).
It is finite and continuous.

For completeness, every combination in
\eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-convex-envelope} can be replaced, without
increasing its value, by one with at most \(d+1\) nonzero coefficients.
Indeed, if there are more, affine dependence gives numbers \(\beta_i\),
not all zero, with
\[
             \sum_i\beta_i=0,\qquad \sum_i\beta_i x_i=0.
\]
Move the weights along one of the two directions
\(\alpha_i+t\beta_i\) for which the objective does not increase, until a
coefficient becomes zero, and iterate.  It follows that the infimum is
attained on a compact parameter space.  If \(x_j\to x\), choose minimizing
representations for \(x_j\) and pass to a convergent subsequence.  The
limiting representation is admissible for \(x\), which proves
\[
 \operatorname{co}_K\phi(x)
 \leq\liminf_j\operatorname{co}_K\phi(x_j).
\]
Thus the envelope is lower semicontinuous.  Convexity follows by combining
two admissible representations.

It remains only to check upper semicontinuity at the boundary of \(K\).
Fix \(x\in K\).  A finite triangulation of \(K\) may be refined so that
\(x\) is a vertex and the closed star of \(x\) is a neighbourhood of
\(x\) in \(K\).  If \(x_j\to x\), pass through the finitely many simplices
of that star.  In a simplex containing \(x\), the barycentric coefficient
of \(x\) tends to one.  Convexity bounds the envelope at \(x_j\) by the
same barycentric combination of its values at \(x\) and at the other
vertices.  The latter values are finite, hence
\[
 \limsup_j\operatorname{co}_K\phi(x_j)
 \leq\operatorname{co}_K\phi(x).
\]
This proves continuity.  Notice that polyhedrality is used exactly in
this boundary argument.

The convexification operation is nonexpanding in the uniform norm:
\begin{equation}
 \left\|\operatorname{co}_K\phi-\operatorname{co}_K\psi\right\|_K
 \leq \|\phi-\psi\|_K .
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-envelope-nonexpanding}
\end{equation}
This follows immediately by applying
\eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-convex-envelope} to the same barycentric
representations in both directions.

\medskip\noindent\emph{Smooth convex majorants on one fixed polytope.}
If \(a:K\to\mathbf R\) is continuous and convex, then for every
\(\varepsilon>0\) there is a smooth convex function \(g\) on the whole
affine span of \(K\) such that
\begin{equation}
                       a\leq g\leq a+\varepsilon
                       \qquad\text{on }K.
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-smooth-majorant}
\end{equation}
To see this, extend \(a\) by \(+\infty\) off \(K\).  The resulting function
is proper, convex, and lower semicontinuous.  Strict separation of its
closed epigraph from the point \((x,a(x)-\delta)\) gives, for every
\(x\in K\) and \(\delta>0\), an affine function \(\ell_x\) such that
\[
                         \ell_x\leq a\text{ on }K,
              \qquad     \ell_x(x)>a(x)-\delta .
\]
The sets on which \(\ell_x>a-\delta\) form an open cover of \(K\).
After taking a finite subcover and putting
\[
                              p=\max_j\ell_{x_j},
\]
we obtain a globally defined convex piecewise-affine function satisfying
\[
                              a-\delta<p\leq a
                              \qquad\text{on }K.
\]
Choose a nonnegative smooth compactly supported probability kernel
\(\rho\) of barycentre zero.  The function \(p\) is globally Lipschitz;
if \(L\) is a Lipschitz constant, then
\[
                  p\leq p*\rho_r\leq p+Lr .
\]
The first inequality is Jensen's inequality.  Taking
\(\delta=\varepsilon/3\), choosing \(r\) with
\(Lr<\varepsilon/3\), and setting
\[
                              g=p*\rho_r+\delta
\]
proves \eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-smooth-majorant}.  If \(L=0\), any
sufficiently small \(r\) works.  This argument is uniform for any finite
family of continuous convex functions by choosing the smoothing radii
separately.

\medskip\noindent
We now turn to the comparison sheaf.  Its defining condition is local, so
it is a sheaf.  Every smooth psh generator belongs to
\(\mathscr C_X\): after a clopen shrinking it is independent of \(z\);
take \(Y\) to be a point.  Positive semidefiniteness of the Hessian implies
convexity on each convex relative neighbourhood in \(P\).

We prove that \(\mathscr C_X\) is stable under decreasing sequential
limits.  Let \(u_n\downarrow u\) on an open subset \(W\subset X\), with
\(u_n\in\mathscr C_X(W)\), and fix \((z_0,x_0)\in W\).  Local compactness
and the clopen basis give a compact clopen neighbourhood \(C\) of \(z_0\).
Choose bounded open polyhedra \(O_1,O_0\subset A\), both containing
\(x_0\), such that
\[
 \overline{O_1}\subset O_0,\qquad
 C\times\bigl(P\cap\overline{O_0}\bigr)\subset W.
\]
After making the polyhedra smaller if necessary, we may and do suppose that
\[
       V=P\cap O_1\quad\text{is convex},\qquad
       K=P\cap\overline{O_0}\quad\text{is a compact convex polytope}.
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-compact-core}
\]

For each fixed \(n\), compactness gives a finite product cover of
\(C\times K\) by sets
\begin{equation}
                           C_{n,a}\times V_{n,a},
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-local-factor-cover}
\end{equation}
where \(C_{n,a}\) is compact clopen in \(C\), \(V_{n,a}\) is relatively
open in \(P\), and on this product \(u_n\) factors through a continuous
surjection
\[
                  q_{n,a}:C_{n,a}\twoheadrightarrow Y_{n,a}
\]
onto a compact metrizable zero-dimensional space.  Choose a countable
clopen base \(\mathcal D_{n,a}\) of each \(Y_{n,a}\).  Let
\(\mathcal B\) be the Boolean subalgebra of the clopen subsets of \(C\)
generated by all \(C_{n,a}\) and all
\[
                     q_{n,a}^{-1}(D),
                     \qquad D\in\mathcal D_{n,a}.
\]
There are only countably many generators.  The evaluation map
\begin{equation}
 q:C\longrightarrow
 Y:=q(C)\subseteq\{0,1\}^{\mathcal B}
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-common-quotient}
\end{equation}
is a continuous surjection onto a compact metrizable zero-dimensional
space.

Every \(u_n|_{C\times V}\) is constant on the fibres of
\(q\times\operatorname{id}_V\).  Indeed, suppose \(q(z)=q(z')\) and
\(x\in V\).  Choose a member of
\eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-local-factor-cover} containing \((z,x)\).
The Boolean coordinates first show that \(z'\in C_{n,a}\), and then that
\(q_{n,a}(z)=q_{n,a}(z')\), since the chosen clopen base separates points.
The local factorization gives \(u_n(z,x)=u_n(z',x)\).  The limit therefore
factors as
\begin{equation}
                           u(z,x)=\bar u(q(z),x)
                           \qquad(C\times V).
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-limit-factor}
\end{equation}

The function \(u\) is upper semicontinuous: each \(u_n\) is locally upper
semicontinuous and
\[
                         \{u<t\}=\bigcup_n\{u_n<t\}.
\]
Upper semicontinuity descends to \(\bar u\) without any unsupported
product-quotient assertion.  If \(\bar u(y,x)<t\), cover the compact fibre
\(q^{-1}(y)\times\{x\}\) by finitely many product neighbourhoods
\(N_j\times D_j\) contained in \(\{u<t\}\).  Set
\(N=\bigcup_jN_j\) and \(D=\bigcap_jD_j\).  Since \(q\) is closed,
\[
                         Y\setminus q(C\setminus N)
\]
is an open neighbourhood of \(y\), and its product with \(D\) lies in
\(\{\bar u<t\}\).

For fixed \(z\), the restrictions \(x\mapsto u_n(z,x)\) are locally
extended-real convex.  The first elementary point makes them convex on
\(V\).  Passing to the limit in every finite convexity inequality shows
that \(x\mapsto u(z,x)\), and hence
\(x\mapsto\bar u(y,x)\), is extended-real convex.  Thus
\(\mathscr C_X\) is decreasing-sequentially closed.  Since it contains
the generators, minimality gives
\begin{equation}
                         \operatorname{Psh}_X\subseteq\mathscr C_X.
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-minimality}
\end{equation}

It remains to prove that every comparison germ is already in the first
stage.  Let \(u\in\mathscr C_X\) have a factorization
\eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-factorization} on \(C\times V_0\).  Choose a
compact convex polytope \(K\subset V_0\) and a relatively open polyhedral
neighbourhood \(V\) of \(x_0\) such that
\begin{equation}
                         \overline V^{\,P}\subset K\subset V_0.
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-nested-core}
\end{equation}
Here the closure is taken in \(P\).  Such a choice is obtained by
intersecting \(P\) with two nested bounded open polyhedral boxes in
\(A\).  We construct every approximant on the one fixed set \(C\times V\).

Give \(Y\times K\) a compatible product metric \(d\).  The upper
semicontinuous function \(\bar u\) is bounded above there; fix an upper
bound \(M\).  For \(k\geq1\), put
\begin{align}
 h_k(s)&=\max\{\bar u(s),-k\},\\
 \Phi_k(s)&=\sup_{t\in Y\times K}
                 \bigl(h_k(t)-k\,d(s,t)\bigr).
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-usc-regularization}
\end{align}
Each \(\Phi_k\) is finite, continuous, and \(k\)-Lipschitz.  Moreover,
\begin{equation}
                \Phi_{k+1}\leq\Phi_k,\qquad
                \Phi_k\geq\bar u,\qquad
                \Phi_k\downarrow\bar u .
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-usc-convergence}
\end{equation}
Only the last assertion requires a check.  Fix \(s\) and a real number
\(a>\bar u(s)\), with \(a\) arbitrary when \(\bar u(s)=-\infty\).
Choose \(b\) with \(\bar u(s)<b<a\).  Upper semicontinuity gives a metric
ball about \(s\) on which \(\bar u<b\).  For large \(k\), also \(-k<b\).
On this ball the expression under the supremum is at most \(b\); outside a
smaller fixed ball it is at most
\(\max\{M,-1\}\) minus \(k\) times a fixed positive number.  It is therefore
less than \(a\) for large \(k\).  This proves the last assertion.

For \(y\in Y\), convexify only in the polyhedral variable:
\begin{equation}
 c_k(y,x)
 =\operatorname{co}_K\bigl(\Phi_k(y,\cdot)\bigr)(x).
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-fibre-convexification}
\end{equation}
Because \(x\mapsto\bar u(y,x)\) is extended-real convex and
\(\bar u\leq\Phi_k\), every barycentric representation of \(x\) gives
\[
       \bar u(y,x)
       \leq\sum_i\alpha_i\bar u(y,x_i)
       \leq\sum_i\alpha_i\Phi_k(y,x_i).
\]
Taking the infimum yields
\begin{equation}
                     \bar u\leq c_k\leq\Phi_k,
        \qquad       c_{k+1}\leq c_k,
        \qquad       c_k\downarrow\bar u .
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-convexified-convergence}
\end{equation}
The function \(c_k\) is jointly continuous on \(Y\times K\).  Continuity
in \(x\) is the second elementary point.  For \(y,y'\in Y\),
\eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-envelope-nonexpanding} and the Lipschitz bound
for \(\Phi_k\) give
\[
 \sup_{x\in K}|c_k(y,x)-c_k(y',x)|
 \leq
 \sup_{x\in K}|\Phi_k(y,x)-\Phi_k(y',x)|
 \leq k\,d_Y(y,y'),
\]
after choosing the product metric in sum form.  Separate continuity with
this uniform estimate gives joint continuity.

Choose nested finite clopen partitions \(\mathcal P_k\) of \(Y\) whose
meshes tend to zero.  Such partitions are obtained by taking finite clopen
covers of successively smaller mesh and refining all preceding covers.
For \(Q\in\mathcal P_k\), set
\begin{equation}
             a_{k,Q}(x)=\max_{y\in Q}c_k(y,x),
             \qquad
             a_k(y,x)=a_{k,Q_k(y)}(x),
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-clopen-envelope}
\end{equation}
where \(Q_k(y)\) is the member containing \(y\).  Each \(a_{k,Q}\) is a
finite continuous convex function on \(K\).  Refinement and
\(c_{k+1}\leq c_k\) give
\begin{equation}
                              a_{k+1}\leq a_k.
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-clopen-monotonicity}
\end{equation}
Furthermore,
\begin{equation}
                              a_k\downarrow\bar u
                              \quad\text{on }Y\times K.
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-clopen-convergence}
\end{equation}
The lower bound follows from \(a_k\geq c_k\geq\bar u\).  For the upper
bound, fix \((y,x)\), choose \(a>\bar u(y,x)\), and then choose
\(b\) strictly between these two numbers.  Choose a metric ball on which
\(\bar u<b\).  For large \(k\), the set \(Q_k(y)\times\{x\}\) lies close
enough to \((y,x)\), and \(-k<b\).  In
\eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-usc-regularization}, points in the chosen ball
contribute at most \(b\), whereas points outside it pay a fixed positive
distance times \(k\).  Consequently
\[
       \sup_{y'\in Q_k(y)}\Phi_k(y',x)<a
\]
for large \(k\).  Since \(a_{k,Q_k(y)}\leq
\sup_{y'\in Q_k(y)}\Phi_k(y',x)\), this proves
\eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-clopen-convergence}, also at a
\(-\infty\)-valued point.

Put \(\varepsilon_k=4^{-k}\).  The smooth-majorant construction, applied
to the finite family indexed by \(\mathcal P_k\), gives smooth convex
functions \(g_{k,Q}\) on \(A\) such that
\begin{equation}
                        a_{k,Q}\leq g_{k,Q}
                        \leq a_{k,Q}+\varepsilon_k
                        \qquad\text{on }K.
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-family-smoothing}
\end{equation}
Define \(w_k\) on \(C\times V\) by
\begin{equation}
                 w_k(z,x)=g_{k,Q}(x)
                 \quad\text{if }q(z)\in Q\in\mathcal P_k.
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-smooth-piecewise}
\end{equation}
The inverse images \(q^{-1}(Q)\) form a finite clopen partition of \(C\)
by subsets which are clopen in \(Z\).  Hence \(w_k\) is smooth for the
stated product structure.  Its Hessian in the \(A\)-directions is positive
semidefinite, so \(w_k\in\operatorname{Psh}_{X,0}(C\times V)\).
Equations \eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-clopen-monotonicity} and
\eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-family-smoothing} imply
\begin{equation}
                             w_{k+1}\leq w_k+\varepsilon_{k+1}.
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-almost-monotone}
\end{equation}

Set
\[
                 \tau_k=\sum_{j\geq k+1}\varepsilon_j,
                 \qquad G_k=w_k+\tau_k .
\]
Since \(\tau_k=\varepsilon_{k+1}+\tau_{k+1}\),
\eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-almost-monotone} gives
\(G_{k+1}\leq G_k\).  Finally,
\eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-clopen-convergence},
\eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-family-smoothing}, and
\(\tau_k\to0\) show that
\[
                         G_k\downarrow u
                         \qquad\text{on }C\times V.
\]
This is \eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-fixed-domain}.  We have proved
\[
                         \mathscr C_X
                         \subseteq\operatorname{Psh}_{X,1}.
\]
Together with \eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-minimality} and the tautological
inclusion
\(\operatorname{Psh}_{X,1}\subseteq\operatorname{Psh}_X\), this proves
\eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-collapse}.

The proof is local and uses only the generator sheaf.  It therefore
transports through any generator-preserving chart and proves the asserted
chartwise extension.  For a rational convex polyhedron with its induced
Chambert--Loir--Ducros affine tropical structure, smooth functions are
locally restrictions of ambient smooth functions; positivity of
\(\mathrm d'\mathrm d''f\) is positive semidefiniteness of the Hessian on
the affine span.  A locally constant affine structure on \(Z\) becomes
constant after a clopen shrinking, and the product construction gives
exactly the generator sheaf used above.  This verifies the claimed
compatibility while leaving untouched the excluded nonconvex and branched
settings.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}
We use the extended-real convention stated before
\Cref{thm:ch16-collapse-finite-tropical-curves}.  The conditions defining
\(\mathcal J_X\) are local.  For the only nonliteral assertion, suppose the
junction inequality holds on an open cover and consider one admissible
tuple.  An open member containing its node contains, for all sufficiently
small \(s>0\), the segments from \((0,y_0)\) to
\[
 \bigl(st_av_{i(a)},\,y_0+s(y_a-y_0)\bigr).
\]
The local junction inequality at these contracted points, followed by
branchwise convexity, gives the asserted inequality after cancelling
\((1-s)u(0,y_0)\) and dividing by \(s\).  The case
\(u(0,y_0)=-\infty\) is automatic.  Thus \(\mathcal J_X\) is a sheaf.
It is closed under pointwise decreasing limits, since both extended-real
convexity and every finite junction inequality pass to such a limit.
Every generator belongs to \(\mathcal J_X\): its ambient affine tangent at
\((0,y_0)\) is a minorant on every branch, and its weighted linear terms
cancel at the displayed barycentre.  Hence
\[
                         \mathcal P_X\subseteq\mathcal J_X.
 \tag{\(\dagger\)}
\]

It remains to prove the reverse inclusion at the first stage.  Away from
\(\{0\}\times P\), this is the one-point case of
\Cref{thm:p071-stone-polyhedral-collapse}, with a singleton clopen
parameter and a sufficiently small convex polyhedral normal-coordinate
interval.  We work at \((0,y_0)\), with \(u\in\mathcal J_X\) defined on
a product neighbourhood.  Choose numbers \(0<2T_i<r_i\), bounded open
polyhedra \(O_1,O_0\subset A\), and put
\[
 V=P\cap O_1,\qquad Q=P\cap\overline{O_0},
\]
so that \(y_0\in V\), \(\overline V^{\,P}\subset Q\), \(Q\) is a
compact convex polytope, and
\[
 D:=\Bigl(\{0\}\cup\coprod_i(0,2T_i]v_i\Bigr)\times Q
\]
is contained in the original domain.  We first construct continuous finite
comparison majorants of \(u|_D\).  This is the step which treats every
polyhedral face and corner.

For a continuous real-valued function \(\phi\) on \(D\), define its
\emph{junction-convex envelope} \(C\phi\) as follows.  At a point
\(x=(tv_i,y)\) with \(t>0\), take the infimum of
\[
                   \sum_a\alpha_a\phi(s_av_{j(a)},y_a)
 \tag{\(\clubsuit\)}
\]
over all finite tuples in \(D\) satisfying
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_a\alpha_a&=1,
 &\sum_a\alpha_as_av_{j(a)}&=tv_i,\\
 \sum_a\alpha_ay_a&=y,
 &\sum_{j(a)=i}\alpha_as_a&\geq t.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{\(\clubsuit_1\)}
\]
At a node \((0,y)\), use the same definition but omit the last inequality;
it is then independent of a branch label.  The singleton tuple shows that
\(C\phi\leq\phi\).

We record the three properties of this envelope needed below.  First,
\(C\phi\) satisfies the two comparison conditions on \(D\).  Indeed,
convex combinations of admissible tuples prove branchwise convexity, and
combining admissible tuples for a balanced node family proves the junction
inequality.  Second, it is the largest function satisfying those conditions
below \(\phi\).  To see this, let \(v\) satisfy them with \(v\leq\phi\),
and consider a tuple in
\((\clubsuit_1)\).  Put
\[
               \lambda=\sum_{j(a)=i}\alpha_as_a\geq t.
\]
For \(t>0\), retain the proportion \(t/\lambda\) of each branch-\(i\)
weight and call all remaining weights residual.  The retained weights have
normal moment \(tv_i\), while the residual weights have normal moment zero.
If the residual mass is nonzero, apply the junction inequality to its
Euclidean barycentre in \(Q\), and then apply branchwise convexity to that
node and the retained branch-\(i\) points.  This gives
\[
                  v(tv_i,y)\leq
                  \sum_a\alpha_av(s_av_{j(a)},y_a).
 \tag{\(\clubsuit_2\)}
\]
If the residual mass is zero, this is ordinary branchwise convexity.  At a
node, \((\clubsuit_2)\) is precisely the junction inequality.  Taking the
infimum proves \(v\leq C\phi\).

Third, \(C\phi\) is finite and continuous on \(D\).  For attainment and
lower semicontinuity, regard the tuples as probability measures on the
compact space \(D\).  Their Euclidean and normal moment constraints are
closed.  The extra branch-\(i\) moment is the integral of the continuous
function which equals \(s\) on branch \(i\), zero on the other branches,
and zero at the common node.  Compactness therefore supplies a minimizing
measure and shows lower semicontinuity under convergent target points; at a
node pass to one of the finitely many branch labels.  Carath\'eodory applied
also to the cost coordinate replaces every minimizing measure by a finite
one, as used in \((\clubsuit)\).  The function \(C\phi\) is finite and
convex on each compact branch prism \([0,2T_i]\times Q\).  A finite convex
function on a compact polytope is upper semicontinuous: triangulate near a
point with that point as a vertex and use the barycentric coefficient tending
to one.  Thus lower and upper semicontinuity give continuity on each branch,
and the common node values glue the finitely many branches continuously.

The restriction to \(D\) of every member of \(\mathcal J_X\) is upper
semicontinuous.  Indeed, \(\max\{u,-N\}\) is finite and satisfies the two
comparison conditions on \(D\): the maximum operation is convex and
nondecreasing, so Jensen's inequality preserves both defining conditions.
It is upper semicontinuous on each compact branch prism by the preceding
polyhedral argument, hence on \(D\); taking the decreasing infimum over
\(N\) proves the assertion for \(u\).

Fix a compatible metric \(d\) on \(D\).  The standard compact-metric
upper regularization
\[
 \phi_n(x):=\sup_{z\in D}
 \left(\max\{u(z),-n\}-n\,d(x,z)\right)
 \tag{\(\clubsuit_3\)}
\]
is finite, continuous, decreases to \(u\), and dominates \(u\).  For the
last assertion, an upper bound for \(u\) on \(D\) and upper
semicontinuity separate a small ball about the chosen point from its compact
complement; the penalty in \((\clubsuit_3)\) then forces convergence.  Set
\[
                              H_n:=C\phi_n.
\]
The preceding three properties give
\[
       u\leq H_n\leq\phi_n,\qquad H_{n+1}\leq H_n,\qquad H_n\downarrow u,
 \tag{\(\clubsuit_4\)}
\]
and every \(H_n\) is finite, continuous, and satisfies the two comparison
conditions on \(D\).

We next give a uniform smooth majorant for one such continuous comparison
function \(H:=H_n\).  Write \(H_i(t,y)=H(tv_i,y)\), including
\(H_i(0,y)=H(0,y)\).  After choosing an origin in \(A\), for
\(p\in A^*\) put
\[
 f_i(t,p)=\min_{y\in Q}\bigl(H_i(t,y)-p\mathbin\cdot y\bigr),
 \qquad
 f_0(p)=\min_{y\in Q}\bigl(H(0,y)-p\mathbin\cdot y\bigr).
 \tag{\(\spadesuit\)}
\]
These are finite continuous scalar star profiles, convex in \(t\), with
common central value \(f_0(p)\).  The product junction inequality proves
their finite-star junction inequalities exactly as follows: for a balanced
normal tuple choose \(y_a\in Q\), put \(\bar y=\sum_a\alpha_ay_a\), and
write
\[
 \begin{split}
 f_0(p)
 &\leq H(0,\bar y)-p\mathbin\cdot\bar y\\
 &\leq\sum_a\alpha_a
      \bigl(H_{i(a)}(t_a,y_a)-p\mathbin\cdot y_a\bigr).
 \end{split}
 \tag{\(\spadesuit_1\)}
\]
Taking independent infima proves the claim.

For every fixed \(t\), the function obtained from \(H_i(t,\cdot)\) by
setting it equal to \(+\infty\) off \(Q\) is proper, lower semicontinuous,
and convex: continuity on the closed polytope is exactly what is needed at
its faces.  Fenchel--Moreau therefore gives, including every boundary point,
\[
 H_i(t,y)=\sup_{p\in A^*}
               \bigl(p\mathbin\cdot y+f_i(t,p)\bigr)
 \qquad (y\in Q).
 \tag{\(\spadesuit_2\)}
\]
Choose nested finite partitions of \([0,2T_i]\), independently of \(p\),
with mesh tending to zero.  Their scalar chordal interpolants
\(h_{\ell,i}(t,p)\) majorize \(f_i(t,p)\), decrease under refinement, and
satisfy the finite-star junction inequalities.  Let
\[
 \widehat H_{\ell,i}(t,y)=
 \sup_p\bigl(p\mathbin\cdot y+h_{\ell,i}(t,p)\bigr).
 \tag{\(\spadesuit_3\)}
\]
The same calculation as in \((\spadesuit_1)\) shows that
\(\widehat H_\ell\) satisfies the two comparison conditions on \(D\).  If
\(t\) lies between adjacent
partition points \(a,b\), with affine weights \(1-\theta,\theta\), then
\[
 H_i(t,y)\leq\widehat H_{\ell,i}(t,y)
 \leq(1-\theta)H_i(a,y)+\theta H_i(b,y).
 \tag{\(\spadesuit_4\)}
\]
Uniform continuity of \(H\) on \(D\) therefore permits a choice of
\(\ell\) for which
\[
                       H\leq\widehat H_\ell\leq H+\varepsilon
 \quad\text{on }D.
 \tag{\(\spadesuit_5\)}
\]
The function \(\widehat H_\ell\) is lower semicontinuous as a supremum and
finite convex on every compact branch prism; the preceding polyhedral
argument makes it continuous on \(D\).

Compactness now yields covectors \(p_1,\ldots,p_q\) such that, with the
middle expression read on branch \(i\),
\[
 \widehat H_\ell-\varepsilon
 \leq A:=\max_j\bigl(p_j\mathbin\cdot y+h_{\ell,i}(t,p_j)\bigr)
 \leq\widehat H_\ell
 \quad\text{on }D.
 \tag{\(\spadesuit_6\)}
\]
For each of the finitely many scalar profiles, the quantitative
common-affine-minorant and regularized-maximum construction in the proof of
\Cref{thm:ch16-collapse-finite-tropical-curves} supplies a smooth ambient
branchwise-convex majorant \(g_j\) on the fixed smaller substar with
\[
                  h_\ell(\cdot,p_j)\leq g_j
                  \leq h_\ell(\cdot,p_j)+\varepsilon.
\]
The functions \(g_j(tv_i)+p_j\mathbin\cdot y\) are ambient-smooth and
jointly convex in \((t,y)\).  Taking their convex coordinatewise
nondecreasing regularized maximum, with error \(\varepsilon\), and adding
one further \(\varepsilon\), gives a function
\(w\in\mathcal G_{X,0}\) on the fixed product
\[
 V_X:=\Bigl(\{0\}\cup\coprod_i(0,\rho_i)v_i\Bigr)\times V,
 \qquad 0<\rho_i<T_i,
\]
such that
\[
                         H\leq w\leq H+4\varepsilon
 \quad\text{on }V_X.
 \tag{\(\spadesuit_7\)}
\]
The affine collar at the common node exists simultaneously because only
finitely many scalar profiles occur; it may depend on \(n\), while the
displayed product neighbourhood does not.  All functions are ambient smooth
in the \(A\)-variables, so this step also applies on every face of \(P\).

Apply this construction to \(H_n\) with a summable positive sequence
\((\varepsilon_n)\), producing \(w_n\) on the one fixed \(V_X\).  Put
\[
 d_n:=4\sum_{k>n}\varepsilon_k,
 \qquad G_n:=w_n+d_n.
\]
Equations \((\clubsuit_4)\) and \((\spadesuit_7)\) give
\[
 G_{n+1}\leq H_{n+1}+4\varepsilon_{n+1}+d_{n+1}
 \leq H_n+d_n\leq G_n.
\]
Since \(H_n\downarrow u\) and \(4\varepsilon_n+d_n\to0\), the sequence
\(G_n\) decreases pointwise to \(u\) on \(V_X\).  Thus
\(\mathcal J_X\subseteq\mathcal P_{X,1}\).  Combining this with
\((\dagger)\) and \(\mathcal P_{X,1}\subseteq\mathcal P_X\) proves the
theorem.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}
Write \(\mathcal J_{S\times P}\) for the comparison sheaf in
\Cref{thm:p071-finite-star-polyhedral-collapse}.  Thus its sections are
exactly the extended-real branchwise jointly convex functions satisfying
the product junction inequalities.  The cited theorem proves three facts
that we use below:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \(\mathcal J_{S\times P}\) is a sheaf, contains the smooth ambient
  generators, and is closed under pointwise decreasing sequential limits;
\item on a compact core
  \[
   D=\Bigl(\{0\}\cup\coprod_i(0,2T_i]v_i\Bigr)\times Q,
  \]
  with \(Q\) a compact convex polytope, the junction-convex envelope of a
  continuous real-valued function is finite, continuous, and is the largest
  comparison function below it;
\item if \(H\) is a continuous real-valued comparison function on \(D\),
  then, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), the construction in the proof of the
  cited theorem gives a smooth ambient generator \(g\) on one prescribed
  smaller product core \(S''\times V'\) such that
  \begin{equation}
                         H\leq g\leq H+4\varepsilon.
   \label{eq:p071-stone-star-one-step-smoothing}
  \end{equation}
  The smaller core depends only on the two nested geometric cores, not on
  \(H\) or \(\varepsilon\).  The construction therefore applies on the
  same smaller core to every member of a finite family.
\end{enumerate}
The third item is the one-step estimate established before the summable
tail correction in that proof; it is stronger than merely invoking the
final sheaf equality.

We first prove that \(\mathcal C_X\) is decreasing-sequentially closed.
Its defining condition is local, and the sheaf property follows from the
sheaf property of \(\mathcal J_{S\times P}\) exactly as for the comparison
sheaf in the finite-star theorem.  Every smooth generator lies in
\(\mathcal C_X\): after a clopen shrinking it is independent of \(z\), so
one takes \(Y\) to be a point.

Let \(u_n\downarrow u\) on an open subset \(W\subset X\), with every
\(u_n\in\mathcal C_X(W)\), and fix a point \((z_0,s_0,y_0)\in W\).
Choose a compact clopen neighbourhood \(C\subset Z\) of \(z_0\) and a
compact finite-star--polytope core \(D_0\subset S\times P\), with the fixed
point in the relative interior appropriate to its stratum, such that
\begin{equation}
                              C\times D_0\subset W.
 \label{eq:p071-stone-star-limit-core}
\end{equation}
If \(s_0\ne0\), use only a compact interval inside its branch.  If
\(s_0=0\), take a positive compact collar in every one of the finitely many
branches.  Shrink once more to a product neighbourhood
\(C\times V_0\) whose closure in \(C\times D_0\) is compact.

For each \(n\), compactness supplies a finite product cover of the latter
closure by sets \(C_{n,a}\times V_{n,a}\), where \(C_{n,a}\) is compact
clopen in \(C\), and on this product \(u_n\) factors through a continuous
surjection
\[
                        q_{n,a}:C_{n,a}\twoheadrightarrow Y_{n,a}
\]
onto a compact metrizable zero-dimensional space.  Choose a countable
clopen base \(\mathcal D_{n,a}\) of every \(Y_{n,a}\).  Let
\(\mathcal B\) be the Boolean subalgebra of the clopen subsets of \(C\)
generated by the sets \(C_{n,a}\) and
\[
                         q_{n,a}^{-1}(D),
                         \qquad D\in\mathcal D_{n,a}.
\]
There are only countably many generators.  The evaluation map
\begin{equation}
 q:C\longrightarrow
 Y:=q(C)\subseteq\{0,1\}^{\mathcal B}
 \label{eq:p071-stone-star-common-quotient}
\end{equation}
is a continuous surjection onto a compact metrizable zero-dimensional
space.

Every \(u_n\) on the smaller product is constant on the fibres of
\(q\times\operatorname{id}\).  Indeed, if \(q(z)=q(z')\), membership in
each \(C_{n,a}\) agrees, while the inverse images of the chosen clopen base
separate the points of \(Y_{n,a}\).  A member of the finite product cover
containing \((z,s,y)\) therefore also contains \((z',s,y)\), and its local
factorization gives \(u_n(z,s,y)=u_n(z',s,y)\).  Passing to the limit gives
\begin{equation}
                        u(z,s,y)=\bar u(q(z),s,y).
 \label{eq:p071-stone-star-limit-factor}
\end{equation}

The function \(\bar u\) is upper semicontinuous.  Indeed,
\(\{u<t\}=\bigcup_n\{u_n<t\}\) is open.  If
\(\bar u(\zeta,s,y)<t\), cover the compact fibre
\(q^{-1}(\zeta)\times\{(s,y)\}\) by finitely many product neighbourhoods
contained in \(\{u<t\}\).  Their finite union in \(C\), their finite
intersection in \(S\times P\), and the open set
\[
                         Y\setminus q(C\setminus N)
\]
give a product neighbourhood of \((\zeta,s,y)\) in
\(\{\bar u<t\}\), because \(q\) is closed.

For a fixed \(z\), every \(u_n(z,\cdot)\) belongs locally to
\(\mathcal J_{S\times P}\).  The sheaf and decreasing-closure properties
recalled in the first item above imply that \(u(z,\cdot)\) does as well.
This property depends only on \(q(z)\), so every fibre
\(\bar u(\zeta,\cdot)\) is a comparison function.  Hence
\(u\in\mathcal C_X\).  We have proved that \(\mathcal C_X\) contains the
generators and is decreasing-sequentially closed.  Minimality gives
\begin{equation}
                          \mathcal P_X\subseteq\mathcal C_X.
 \label{eq:p071-stone-star-minimality}
\end{equation}

It remains to place every comparison germ in the first stage.  Away from
the node this follows from
\Cref{thm:p071-stone-polyhedral-collapse}, after using a compact interval
in the branch together with \(P\) as one convex polyhedron.  We therefore
work at \((z_0,0,y_0)\).  Let \(u\in\mathcal C_X\) have the factorization
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-star-factorization} on
\(C\times S'\times V_0\), and write
\[
                  S'=\{0\}\cup\coprod_i(0,r_i')v_i.
\]
Choose numbers
\[
                   0<\rho_i<T_i<2T_i<r_i'
\]
inside the available branch collars, a compact convex polytope
\(Q\subset V_0\), and a relatively open polyhedral neighbourhood
\(V'\ni y_0\) such that \(\overline{V'}^{\,P}\subset Q\).  Put
\begin{equation}
 D=\Bigl(\{0\}\cup\coprod_i(0,2T_i]v_i\Bigr)\times Q,
 \qquad
 D'=\Bigl(\{0\}\cup\coprod_i(0,\rho_i)v_i\Bigr)\times V'.
 \label{eq:p071-stone-star-nested-cores}
\end{equation}
Both cores are fixed for the rest of the proof.

Give \(Y\times D\) a compatible product metric \(d\).  The upper
semicontinuous function \(\bar u\) is bounded above there.  For \(k\geq1\)
set
\begin{align}
 h_k(\xi)&=\max\{\bar u(\xi),-k\},\\
 \Phi_k(\xi)&=\sup_{\eta\in Y\times D}
                 \bigl(h_k(\eta)-k\,d(\xi,\eta)\bigr).
 \label{eq:p071-stone-star-usc-regularization}
\end{align}
Then \(\Phi_k\) is finite, continuous, and \(k\)-Lipschitz, and
\begin{equation}
               \Phi_{k+1}\leq\Phi_k,
        \qquad \Phi_k\geq\bar u,
        \qquad \Phi_k\downarrow\bar u.
 \label{eq:p071-stone-star-usc-convergence}
\end{equation}
The convergence is the standard compact-metric upper regularization
argument: an upper-semicontinuity neighbourhood controls nearby points,
and the term \(-k\,d\) sends the compact complement below any prescribed
upper level.

For \(\zeta\in Y\), apply the junction-convex envelope from the second
item above only in the \(D\)-variable:
\begin{equation}
                    c_k(\zeta,\cdot)
          =C_D\bigl(\Phi_k(\zeta,\cdot)\bigr).
 \label{eq:p071-stone-star-fibre-envelope}
\end{equation}
Every \(c_k(\zeta,\cdot)\) is a finite continuous comparison function.
Because \(\bar u(\zeta,\cdot)\) is a comparison function below
\(\Phi_k(\zeta,\cdot)\), maximality of the envelope gives
\begin{equation}
       \bar u\leq c_k\leq\Phi_k,
       \qquad c_{k+1}\leq c_k,
       \qquad c_k\downarrow\bar u.
 \label{eq:p071-stone-star-envelope-convergence}
\end{equation}

We record the parameter continuity, since it is what makes the Stone
discretization legitimate.  The envelope is nonexpanding in the uniform
norm:
\begin{equation}
 \lVert C_D\phi-C_D\psi\rVert_D
       \leq\lVert\phi-\psi\rVert_D.
 \label{eq:p071-stone-star-envelope-nonexpanding}
\end{equation}
Indeed, if the norm on the right is \(\delta\), then
\(C_D\phi-\delta\) is a comparison function below \(\psi\), whence
\(C_D\phi-\delta\leq C_D\psi\); interchange \(\phi\) and \(\psi\).
The Lipschitz estimate for \(\Phi_k\) and
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-star-envelope-nonexpanding} show that \(c_k\) is
jointly continuous on \(Y\times D\).

Choose nested finite clopen partitions \(\mathscr P_k\) of \(Y\) whose
meshes tend to zero.  For \(R\in\mathscr P_k\), define
\begin{equation}
 a_{k,R}(s,y)=\max_{\zeta\in R}c_k(\zeta,s,y),
 \qquad
 a_k(\zeta,s,y)=a_{k,R_k(\zeta)}(s,y).
 \label{eq:p071-stone-star-clopen-envelope}
\end{equation}
The maximum is attained and \(a_{k,R}\) is continuous.  It is also a
comparison function: a supremum of branchwise jointly convex functions is
branchwise jointly convex, and applying each junction inequality before
taking the supremum gives
\[
 \sup_{\zeta\in R}c_k(\zeta,0,y_*)
 \leq \sum_a\alpha_a
          \sup_{\zeta\in R}c_k(\zeta,t_av_{i(a)},y_a).
\]
Refinement and \(c_{k+1}\leq c_k\) imply
\begin{equation}
                             a_{k+1}\leq a_k.
 \label{eq:p071-stone-star-clopen-monotonicity}
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
                             a_k\downarrow\bar u
                             \quad\text{on }Y\times D.
 \label{eq:p071-stone-star-clopen-convergence}
\end{equation}
The lower bound follows from
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-star-envelope-convergence}.  For the upper bound, at a
fixed \((\zeta,s,y)\) use
\[
 a_k(\zeta,s,y)
 \leq\max_{\zeta'\in R_k(\zeta)}
              \Phi_k(\zeta',s,y).
\]
The shrinking mesh and the compact-metric argument for
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-star-usc-convergence} make the right-hand side tend to
\(\bar u(\zeta,s,y)\), including when that value is \(-\infty\).

Fix positive numbers \(\varepsilon_k\) with
\(\sum_k\varepsilon_k<\infty\).  For each \(k\), apply the one-step
smoothing estimate
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-star-one-step-smoothing} to the finite family
\(\{a_{k,R}:R\in\mathscr P_k\}\).  We obtain smooth ambient generators
\(g_{k,R}\) on the one fixed core \(D'\) such that
\begin{equation}
                 a_{k,R}\leq g_{k,R}
                    \leq a_{k,R}+4\varepsilon_k.
 \label{eq:p071-stone-star-family-smoothing}
\end{equation}
Define on \(C\times D'\)
\begin{equation}
 w_k(z,s,y)=g_{k,R}(s,y)
       \quad\text{when }q(z)\in R\in\mathscr P_k.
 \label{eq:p071-stone-star-piecewise-smoothing}
\end{equation}
The inverse images \(q^{-1}(R)\) form a finite clopen partition of \(C\),
so \(w_k\in\mathcal G_{X,0}(C\times D')\).  Equations
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-star-clopen-monotonicity} and
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-star-family-smoothing} give
\begin{equation}
                         w_{k+1}\leq w_k+4\varepsilon_{k+1}.
 \label{eq:p071-stone-star-almost-monotone}
\end{equation}

Set
\[
                    \tau_k=4\sum_{j>k}\varepsilon_j,
                    \qquad G_k=w_k+\tau_k.
\]
Since \(\tau_k=4\varepsilon_{k+1}+\tau_{k+1}\),
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-star-almost-monotone} gives
\(G_{k+1}\leq G_k\).  Equations
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-star-clopen-convergence} and
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-star-family-smoothing}, together with
\(\tau_k\to0\), give
\[
                              G_k\downarrow u
                              \qquad\text{on }C\times D'.
\]
Thus \(\mathcal C_X\subseteq\mathcal P_{X,1}\).  Combining this with
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-star-minimality} and the tautological inclusion
\(\mathcal P_{X,1}\subseteq\mathcal P_X\) proves
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-star-collapse} and the fixed-neighbourhood assertion.
The final scope statement is immediate from the hypotheses: the Stone
factor is used only through clopen partitions, the star is finite and
ambient-induced, and the entire \(P\)-factor lies in one convex chamber.
\end{proof}
